attributes.residual: RE-TYPED FROM ALLOCATOR NOISE TO ONE REPEATED ADDRESSING FORM. regnorm: 5 renaming, 6 STRUCTURAL, 0 UNPAIRED, and all six rows are the same shape repeated three times. Target: `add r4,r5,r3` then `stw r0,DISP(r4)` - it forms the element address once and stores at a constant member displacement. Ours: `addi r0,r3,DISP` then `stwx r4,r5,r0` - it folds the member displacement into the index and uses an indexed store. The three sites carry DISP 2860 (+0x0018/+0x001c), 1324 (+0x0038/+0x003c) and 1176 (+0x0058/+0x005c). This is a source-reachable addressing-form difference: the target's shape is what `base[i].member = x` on a properly typed array yields, while the indexed form is what raw pointer arithmetic over a byte cursor yields, so this function is also de-fakematch debt. THE SAME FORM APPEARS IN fn_80051164 (game/game/gamemain, 2 STRUCTURAL rows, 0 unpaired: target `add r4,r7,r3` + `stw r0,32(r4)`, ours `addi r0,r3,32` + `stwx r4,r6,r0`), so a single typed-array conversion recipe should close both; they are the two cheapest members of this class in the census.
